harmonicFunction: G6 (I6) - Tonic with added 6th giving a bittersweet, complex character
Bb6 (bIII6) - Chromatic mediant chord creating surreal tonal shift
F5 (bVII5) - Power chord on the flat seventh for rock tension
Em (vi) - Relative minor providing brief diatonic stability
Eb (bVI) - Chromatic chord a half step below Em, adding dissonance
Ab (bII) - Neapolitan-influenced chord in the chorus for dramatic effect
D (V) - Dominant chord providing rare moments of traditional resolution

techniques.name: Unusual Chord Voicings
techniques.description: Non-standard chord shapes including 6th chords, chromatic voicings, and open-string combinations that create the song's distinctive harmonic palette

notes: G6: 3-2-0-0-0-0 (uses open strings for full, ringing voicing)
Bb6: X-1-3-0-3-0 (open string voicing with barre elements)
F5: 1-3-3-X-X-X (power chord at 1st fret)
Em: 0-2-2-0-0-0 (standard open voicing)
Eb: X-6-5-3-4-3 or X-X-1-3-4-3 (barre voicing)
Ab: 4-6-6-5-4-4 (barre chord at 4th fret)
Many voicings use open strings for a unique, ringing quality
sequence: Learn each chord shape individually, checking that all notes ring cleanly
Practice the G6 to Bb6 transition - this is the most unusual movement
Work on the chromatic descent: F5 to Em to Eb
Connect the verse progression in sequence at a very slow tempo
Add the chorus chords: G - Ab - A - C progression
tips: Many of these chords use open strings - let them ring for the full effect
The transitions between chromatic chords require careful finger positioning
Don't try to use standard chord shapes - the song requires specific voicings
The slow tempo (52 BPM) gives you time to make each chord change cleanly
Practice the unusual shapes until they become muscle memory

techniques.name: Whammy Bar Vibrato
techniques.description: Using the tremolo bar for wide, slow vibrato on sustained notes and chords, adding the song's signature eerie, wavering quality

notes: Apply slow, wide vibrato to sustained chord hits for a woozy effect
The whammy bar dip and return should be slow and controlled
Use the bar on held notes in the verse for atmospheric texture
Chris Cornell's guitar parts use subtle bar work throughout
The effect creates the psychedelic, underwater quality of the song
sequence: Strum a chord and let it ring
Apply gentle downward pressure on the whammy bar
Slowly return to pitch, creating a wide vibrato effect
Repeat the motion 2-3 times per sustained chord
Use sparingly - too much vibrato breaks the mood
tips: A floating tremolo bridge (Floyd Rose or Fender) works best
If your guitar has a fixed bridge, skip this technique and focus on finger vibrato
The vibrato speed should match the slow tempo - no rapid shaking
Practice controlling the depth of the vibrato for musical expression
Combine with the chorus effect for maximum atmospheric impact
details.progression: Applied over sustained chord hits in the verse

techniques.name: Dynamic Control
techniques.description: Managing the extreme dynamic range from whisper-quiet verses to the massive, explosive chorus, requiring precise control of picking intensity and volume

notes: Verses should be played softly with restrained strumming
Pre-chorus builds gradually in volume and intensity
Chorus reaches full volume with aggressive strumming
The quiet-to-loud arc repeats with each verse-chorus cycle
Use the guitar volume knob to assist with dynamic transitions
sequence: Start the verse at approximately 40% volume with gentle picking
Gradually increase volume through the pre-chorus to 70%
Hit the chorus at full 100% intensity with aggressive strumming
Pull back dramatically for the return to verse at 40%
Each verse-chorus cycle can build slightly louder than the previous one
tips: The dynamic range is what makes this song emotionally powerful
Practice playing very quietly without losing clarity or note definition
Use picking angle and distance from the bridge to control tone and volume
The transition points between sections should feel natural, not abrupt
Record yourself to verify that the dynamic contrast is audible

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The intro establishes the song's surreal harmonic language with the clean G6 chord arpeggiated slowly, setting the psychedelic mood before the full band enters
notes: Let the G6 chord ring fully - the open strings create a shimmering effect
The transition to Bb6 is the first hint of the song's chromatic language
Play at a very slow, deliberate pace matching the 52 BPM tempo
The intro is clean-toned with subtle reverb

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse cycles through the chromatic chord progression with soft, controlled strumming, creating the song's hypnotic and slightly unsettling atmosphere
notes: Keep the dynamics soft during the verse - restraint is key
Let each chord ring and breathe before moving to the next
The chromatic movement from Em to Eb is a half-step descent - voice it smoothly
Apply subtle whammy bar vibrato on sustained chords for atmosphere

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.description: The pre-chorus builds tension with rising intensity, moving through D-Eb-G-F-Em-Eb with increasing strumming aggression leading into the explosive chorus
sections.progression: D - Eb - G - F - Em - Eb
notes: Gradually increase volume and intensity through the pre-chorus
The D to Eb movement (half step up) creates rising tension
Strum harder and use more aggressive picking as the section progresses
The final Eb chord should be at the threshold of the chorus volume

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus erupts with full-volume power chord strumming, the chromatic G-Ab-A ascent creating the songthe iconic vocal hookblack hole sun, wonthe iconic vocal hook
sections.progression: G - Ab - A - C - Eb - D
notes: Full volume and intensity - this is the emotional peak of the song
The chromatic walk from G through Ab to A is the signature chorus movement
Use full barre chord or power chord voicings for maximum impact
The vocal melody soars here - the guitar must match that emotional energy

sections.name: Solo
sections.description: Kim Thayil's guitar solo combines pentatonic-based phrases with chromatic runs and extensive whammy bar work, creating an otherworldly and emotionally intense passage
notes: The solo uses the G minor pentatonic and chromatic passing tones
Whammy bar dives and wide vibrato give the solo its eerie character
Bends are slow and deliberate, matching the song's tempo
This is an advanced section - beginners can skip the solo initially

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The outro builds to the song's final massive climax, repeating the chorus progression with increasing intensity before resolving with a sustained, feedback-drenched chord
notes: The outro is the most intense section of the entire song
Each repetition of the chorus progression builds in volume and aggression
Allow controlled feedback on the final sustained chord
The ending should feel cathartic and emotionally overwhelming

guitar.recommended: Guild S-100 or similar semi-hollow body
alternatives: Any guitar with humbuckers and a whammy bar
guitar.pickup: Humbuckers for thick, warm sustain; neck pickup for clean sections, bridge for distorted

settings.presence: 6 (cut through the mix in chorus sections)

effects.distortion: Medium gain overdrive/distortion for chorus, clean for verse; not too heavy
effects.reverb: Moderate hall reverb for atmospheric space and depth
effects.other: Whammy bar on the guitar for vibrato effects; optional chorus or phaser for psychedelic texture on clean sections

beginner.focus: Learn the basic chord shapes and understand the unusual harmonic movement
steps: Learn the G6, Em, and D chord shapes as the simplest starting points
Practice the F5 power chord shape and Eb barre chord
Study the chord chart to understand which chords go where in the song
Strum through the verse progression very slowly, one chord at a time

intermediate.focus: Master all chord voicings and develop the dynamic control between sections
steps: Learn all the unusual voicings including Bb6 and the chorus chords
Practice transitions between the chromatic chords at slow tempo
Work on the dynamic arc from quiet verse to loud chorus
Play through the complete song structure with proper section transitions

advanced.focus: Add the solo, whammy bar work, and achieve the authentic atmospheric tone
steps: Learn the guitar solo using pentatonic scales and chromatic passing tones
Master whammy bar vibrato for atmospheric chord sustains
Dial in the precise tone for each section (clean, crunch, distorted)
Perform the entire 5+ minute song with full dynamic and emotional range

commonMistakes: Treating the chromatic chords as mistakes - they are intentional and essential
Playing at a constant volume instead of utilizing the extreme dynamic range
Rushing the tempo - 52 BPM is very slow and requires patience and discipline
Using too much gain which blurs the chord voicings and eliminates dynamic range
practiceRoutine: Warm up with the unusual chord shapes individually for 5 minutes each
Practice the verse chord progression (G6-Bb6-F5-Em-Eb) at 40 BPM
Work on the pre-chorus build-up focusing on gradual dynamic increase
Practice the chorus at full volume with aggressive strumming confidence
Play through the entire song from start to finish, focusing on dynamics
focusAreas: Accurate fingering for unusual chord voicings (G6, Bb6 especially)
Dynamic control across the extreme quiet-to-loud range
Patient tempo discipline at the slow 52 BPM
Smooth chromatic chord transitions without stumbling
metronomeWork: Start at 40 BPM to internalize the very slow pulse
Practice chord changes at 45 BPM with one chord per measure
Work up to 52 BPM (song tempo) with the complete verse progression
At 52 BPM, add dynamic markings: piano for verse, forte for chorus
